answer: A radio-ranging protocol limits Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to multipath RF reflections from a stationary beacon situated in an open meadow. A verifier analyzes the returned electromagnetic echo to confirm the agent's unique physical antenna location. An attacker must purchase and position dedicated transceiver hardware per identity rather than multiplexing virtual nodes. However, moving foliage and weather shifts can perturb signal paths, falsely rejecting legitimate agents.
